newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Powerfin shareholders eye Tractebel deal.
newsitem.headline: Powerfin shareholders eye Tractebel deal.

text.p: A full merger between Belgium's dominant utility holding company Tractebel and its main foreign energy unit Powerfin will put the group on course for an international future, analysts said on Tuesday.
"Internationalisation is part of (Tractebel's) strategy," utilities analyst at Generale Bank Securities Sandra Vandermissen told Reuters.
Tractebel's board of directors looks set to decide on Thursday whether to absorb Powerfin.
Analysts already took the move for granted. The question now was when the deal would take place and how would shares be transferred and when Powerfin would be delisted.

"If the decision is taken on Thursday I believe it will come into effect after Christmas, because launching such a big operation wouldn't work over Christmas," analyst Maud Watelet brokers Mignon Hanart Declerck said.

Powerfin was set up to spearhead Tractebel's expansion drive in the electricity sector abroad. In Belgium Tractebel's role as the main shareholder in Electrabel gives it a virtual monopoly in energy production.
The merger would give Tractebel, which owns about 60 percent of Powerfin, all Powerfin earnings and complete access to Powerfin's international market.
The Powerfin freefloat was valued at about 38 billion Belgian francs ($1.2 billion) this summer.
Analysts said the merger would not be a walkover for the board as Powerfin shareholders could put up a fight if they were not adequately rewarded for swapping their shares.

"I hope they will be given a better ratio than three Powerfin shares for one Tractebel share because Powerfin was such a good company and such a good share that shareholders should be compensated," Watelet said.

A weekend report in the Belgian financial daily De Financieel- Economische Tijd said the terms of exchange would be three for one, valuing one Powerfin share at 4,850 Belgian francs, matching its market price on Tuesday.
Powerfin shares have been rising since January 1995 when they were at 2,800 francs. In the year to date Powerfin rose 25.5 percent. The bourse's Bel-20 index rose 20.9 percent.
Tractebel shares stood at 14,550 francs on Tuesday. By contrast, the stock has underperformed the bourse index, gaining only 17.7 percent in the year to date.

Vandermissen said, "We have a 'hold' on Tractebel because in the medium term it does not look like it will outperform the market." She expected Tractebel to give Powerfin shareholders a better deal than three for one, probably in the form of additional cash or put warrants.
"Today there is so much opposition from major shareholders in the UK and in Belgium that they will join forces and vote against a Tractebel move if it does not favour them," she said.
Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) owns 65 percent of Tractebel. Analysts said the proposed merger with Powerfin would reduce its stake to 53 to 54 percent.
Analysts said Powerfin's strong performance abroad would be diluted by the merger into the larger Tractebel group, where its earnings would be used to offset weaker divisions, such as real estate.
A delisting of Powerfin would protect the firm from having to make public sensitive information which competitors could benefit from, analysts noted. ($ = 32 Belgian Francs)
